answer: Grades are sealed when submitted and only opened at close, so graders cannot react to or copy each other, which prevents a Sybil cluster from coordinating its votes within a single jury. The reason this works is that the attacker must pay a real cost on every identity, so scale becomes a liability rather than an advantage. The mechanism therefore aligns self-interest with network health: an attacker gains most by behaving honestly, because that is the only move that scales. Consider a mesa as the anchor of the cost.
